We stated in our last, in reference to the excessive heat of the 16th, 17th, and 18th days of this month, that thermometer stood from 85 to 90. We have now good authority, to two cases for say ing, that on the north side of building, and on the same side of tree, in this town, it stood at 90 at half past 2 p. m. We understand 90 to be the greatest degree of heat recorded before in this vicinity, and as evidence of the extraordinary heat of the above days, we learn that a great number of beehives are entirely destroyed by the melting of the comb, whereby the honey was entirely lost, and great number of bees drowned. This is circumstance we do not recollect ever having heard of before. We have witnessed the adore disaster to the bees in one instance in this village, where the honey had been entirely dislodged from the hive, by the excessive heat of the 18th.
